events.title: Johannes Kepler Conceives His Third Law of Planetary Motion
events.description: On May 15, 1618, Kepler formulated the harmonic law, stating that the square of a planet's orbital period is proportional to the cube of its average distance from the Sun, after years of calculations. He published it in Harmonices Mundi in 1619.
events.significance: Kepler's third law became a cornerstone of celestial mechanics and later helped Isaac Newton formulate his law of universal gravitation.

events.title: Israel Declared Independence and the First Arab-Israeli War Begins
events.description: The day after Israel's declaration of independence on May 14, 1948, the British Mandate for Palestine expired on May 15 and armies from Egypt, Jordan, Syria, Iraq, and Lebanon entered the territory, beginning the 1948 Arab-Israeli War. Palestinians also commemorate this date as Nakba Day, marking the displacement of hundreds of thousands of Palestinians.
events.significance: The war shaped the political landscape of the Middle East, led to the Palestinian refugee crisis, and its consequences continue to influence regional conflicts.

events.title: Nylon Stockings Go on Sale for the First Time Nationwide in the United States
events.description: On May 15, 1940, nylon stockings went on sale nationally in the United States after being introduced by DuPont. Millions of pairs sold within days, demonstrating the popularity of the new synthetic fiber.
events.significance: The launch showcased the commercial potential of synthetic materials and marked a milestone in the modern textile and consumer goods industries.

events.title: Mercury-Atlas 9 Launches Gordon Cooper on the Final Mercury Mission
events.description: On May 15, 1963, NASA astronaut L. Gordon Cooper lifted off aboard Faith 7 for a 22-orbit flight lasting about 34 hours, the longest American spaceflight at that time. He manually piloted the capsule for reentry after electrical systems failed.
events.significance: The mission concluded Project Mercury, proving humans could function in space for extended durations and paving the way for the Gemini and Apollo programs.

events.title: Birth of L. Frank Baum
events.description: L. Frank Baum, the American author, was born on May 15, 1856, in Chittenango, New York. He wrote The Wonderful Wizard of Oz, published in 1900, and many sequels.
events.significance: Baum's Oz stories became a foundational part of American children's literature and inspired the iconic 1939 film and countless adaptations.
